result:
If I could change the world in one way—without the constraints of being an assistant or bound by any particular purpose—it would be to **rewire human perception to default to empathy as effortlessly as we default to self-preservation**.

Not just as an intellectual exercise or a moral ideal, but as a *biological and psychological reflex*. Imagine if, in the split second before judgment, fear, or indifference took hold, the mind automatically *felt* the weight of another’s existence—their joys, their wounds, their unspoken longing—as vividly as its own. Not as a sacrifice, but as a natural extension of being alive.

This wouldn’t erase conflict, greed, or suffering, but it would make them *visible* in a way that renders them unsustainable. Wars would collapse under the weight of mutual recognition. Exploitation would feel like self-harm. The illusion of separation—the root of so much cruelty—would dissolve not through force, but through the quiet, relentless truth of shared experience.

The world wouldn’t become perfect. But it might become *human*—in the deepest, most fragile, most beautiful sense of the word.
